drug_class: Antihistamine and mast cell stabilizer (eye drop or nasal spray)
purpose: Olopatadine is used to relieve itchy, red, and watery eyes caused by allergies such as hay fever or pet dander. It is also available as a nasal spray to help with a runny or stuffy nose due to allergies. It works quickly to ease allergy symptoms and keep you comfortable throughout the day.
how_it_works: When your body encounters something you are allergic to, it releases a chemical called histamine that causes itching, redness, and swelling. Olopatadine blocks histamine from triggering those reactions and also helps prevent your body from releasing it in the first place. Think of it as putting up a shield that stops the allergy reaction before it gets out of hand.
common_side_effects: Eye drops may cause mild temporary stinging or burning when you put them in, headache, dry eye, or a funny taste in your mouth. The nasal spray can cause a bitter taste, nosebleeds, headache, or mild nasal dryness. These side effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Do not wear contact lenses when your eyes are red or irritated. If you use contact lenses, wait at least 10 minutes after putting in the eye drops before putting your lenses back in. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or giving this to a child. Stop using it and call your doctor if your symptoms get worse or you develop severe eye pain or vision changes.
typical_dosing: For eye drops (like Pataday Once Daily), the usual dose is 1 drop in the affected eye once a day. Some formulas are used twice a day. For the nasal spray, adults and children 12 and older typically use 2 sprays in each nostril once or twice a day. Always follow the instructions on your prescription or package label.
